## Purpose

This procedure orients new personnel to the Bio-Rad QX200 Droplet Digital PCR
(ddPCR) system and describes its safe, standard operation: the components of
the system, the consumables and reagents, the four-stage workflow (droplet
generation, plate sealing, thermal cycling, and droplet reading), basic use of
QuantaSoft software, routine maintenance, and common troubleshooting.

It is a familiarization and operation SOP. It does not cover the science of
assay or primer design (see
[SOP-L701](SOP-L701-ddpcr-nitrogen-cycle-primers.qmd)) or the analysis and
interpretation of results (see
[SOP-L702 Applications Guide](SOP-L702-ddpcr-applications-guide.qmd)). The
workflow described here follows Bio-Rad's published guidance for the platform
[@biorad_appsguide2018; @biorad_qx200_2024], which itself implements the
droplet-counting principle of absolute quantification [@hindson2011].


## Scope

- **Applies to:** Operation of the QX200 ddPCR system in the lab, comprising
  the QX200 Droplet Generator, the PX1 PCR Plate Sealer, the C1000 Touch
  Thermal Cycler with 96-deep-well reaction module, and the QX200 Droplet
  Reader, together with QuantaSoft software.
- **Does not apply to:** Assay/primer design (SOP-L701), data analysis and
  interpretation (SOP-L702), or DNA extraction (SOP-L700).
- **Prerequisite:** A prepared, validated reaction mix and plate plan from
  SOP-L701.

::: {.callout-note}
### SOP numbering
This instrument SOP is numbered L214, placing it ahead of the L700-series
analysis SOPs in the lab scheme. Conceptually it precedes analysis: complete
this familiarization before running samples for SOP-L702.
:::


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                                          |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI            | Approve instrument access; oversee major maintenance    |
| Lab Manager       | Maintain consumable stock, oil, and service records     |
| Trained Personnel | Operate the system per this SOP; log each run           |
| New Students      | Complete familiarization and supervised runs before independent use |


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards and precautions

- **Droplet generation oil and reader oil.** Use the oil specified for the
  chemistry (probe vs. EvaGreen). Avoid skin and eye contact; wear gloves and
  eye protection; consult the SDS for each oil. Clean spills promptly.
- **Reagents.** ddPCR supermixes and any sample DNA are handled with gloves.
  Environmental soil DNA is low biohazard risk, but treat all extracts with
  standard lab precautions.
- **Moving parts.** The droplet reader autosampler moves during a run. Keep
  hands clear and the lid closed while running.
- **Electrical and thermal.** Standard bench-instrument electrical safety. The
  thermal cycler block reaches high temperatures; do not touch the block
  during or immediately after a run.
- **Sharps / glass.** None in normal operation; cartridges and plates are
  single-use plastics.
:::

::: {.callout-important}
### Consumables are not interchangeable
ddPCR requires Bio-Rad's proprietary droplet-generation reagents, cartridges,
and gaskets. Substituting non-specified consumables will produce unusable
droplets [@biorad_appsguide2018]. Match the oil to the supermix chemistry.
:::


## Equipment, Consumables, and Reagents

### Instruments

| Item                                  | Role in workflow                              |
|:--------------------------------------|:----------------------------------------------|
| QX200 Droplet Generator               | Partitions each 20 uL reaction into ~20,000 droplets |
| DG8 cartridge holder                  | Holds the DG8 cartridge during generation     |
| PX1 PCR Plate Sealer                  | Heat-seals droplets into the 96-well plate with pierceable foil |
| C1000 Touch Thermal Cycler (96-deep-well module) | Endpoint PCR amplification within droplets |
| QX200 Droplet Reader                  | Streams droplets single-file and reads two-color fluorescence |
| Instrument computer (QuantaSoft)      | Plate setup, run control, thresholding, export |

### Consumables and reagents

| Item                                       | Notes                                   |
|:-------------------------------------------|:----------------------------------------|
| DG8 cartridges and gaskets                 | Single-use; one cartridge = 8 samples   |
| Droplet generation oil (probes) **or** QX200 EvaGreen droplet oil | Match to supermix chemistry |
| Droplet reader oil                         | Loaded in the reader                    |
| ddPCR Supermix for Probes **or** QX200 ddPCR EvaGreen Supermix | Per assay (SOP-L701) |
| ddPCR 96-well plates and pierceable foil heat seals | For PX1 sealing and reading      |
| Filtered pipette tips, low-bind tubes      | Standard molecular-biology consumables  |

::: {.callout-tip}
Keep a stock log for cartridges, gaskets, oils, plates, and foil. The droplet
generator and reader each draw oil from onboard bottles; check levels before
every session.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
### Ordering supermixes, oils, and assays
Order supermixes, droplet oils, cartridges, plates, and validated PrimePCR
ddPCR assays from the Bio-Rad digital assay catalog:
<https://www.bio-rad.com/digital-assays>. Confirm chemistry (probe vs
EvaGreen) before ordering so the supermix and matching oil are consistent.
:::


## Procedure

### System Overview

The QX200 system performs absolute quantification by partitioning, amplifying,
and counting [@biorad_appsguide2018; @hindson2011]. A single 20 uL reaction is
split into roughly 20,000 uniform water-in-oil droplets. Each droplet is a
tiny independent PCR. After endpoint amplification, the reader passes droplets
one at a time through a two-color optical detector (channel 1 for FAM, channel
2 for HEX or VIC), scoring each droplet as positive or negative. QuantaSoft
fits the positive fraction to a Poisson model to return target concentration
in copies per microliter.

The work proceeds through four instruments in sequence:

1. **Droplet Generator** (Section 6.4) makes the droplets.
2. **PX1 Plate Sealer** (Section 6.5) seals them into a plate.
3. **C1000 Touch Thermal Cycler** (Section 6.6) amplifies.
4. **Droplet Reader** (Section 6.7) counts.

### Daily Startup

1. Power on the instrument computer and the instruments to be used.
2. Launch QuantaSoft and confirm it connects to the droplet generator and/or
   reader.
3. Check oil levels in the droplet generator and the reader; top up or replace
   bottles per the manual [@biorad_qx200_2024].
4. Empty the reader's waste bottle if near full.
5. Confirm consumable stock for the planned run (cartridges, gaskets, oil,
   plate, foil).

### Consumables Orientation

Before the first run, identify each consumable and where it loads:

- **DG8 cartridge** seats in the cartridge holder. The middle row of wells
  receives sample; the bottom row receives generation oil; the top row
  collects the generated droplets.
- **Gasket** snaps over the loaded cartridge to seal it for generation.
- **Generation oil** is chemistry-specific. Using probe oil with EvaGreen
  supermix (or vice versa) will fail.
- **Pierceable foil** is the only seal type compatible with the reader's
  autosampler; do not use hard-seal films.

### Droplet Generation

1. Prepare reactions per SOP-L701 and load into the cartridge holder with a
   DG8 cartridge.
2. Pipette each sample into the sample wells (avoid bubbles; pipette to the
   first stop).
3. Pipette the matched generation oil into the oil wells.
4. Place the gasket over the cartridge.
5. Load the holder into the QX200 Droplet Generator and close the lid; the run
   takes about two minutes per cartridge.
6. After generation, slowly transfer the droplets from the top row of the
   cartridge to the corresponding wells of a ddPCR 96-well plate using a
   multichannel pipette. Pipette gently and at an angle; droplets are fragile
   and shearing them lowers the usable count.

::: {.callout-warning}
Damaged or sheared droplets reduce accepted-droplet counts and can fail the QC
threshold (see SOP-L702, Section 6.2). Pipette droplets slowly and avoid
introducing air.
:::

### Plate Sealing (PX1)

1. Place the plate and a sheet of pierceable foil in the PX1 Plate Sealer.
2. Seal at the manufacturer-specified temperature and time (commonly 180 C for
   5 s; confirm against the current manual [@biorad_qx200_2024]).
3. Inspect the seal: the foil should be uniformly bonded with no lifted edges.

### PCR Amplification

1. Transfer the sealed plate to the C1000 Touch with the 96-deep-well module.
2. Run the validated cycling program for the assay (from SOP-L701).
3. **Set the ramp rate to about 2 C/s.** This slower ramp is important for
   even amplification across the droplet population on this platform
   [@biorad_appsguide2018].
4. Include a final hold and store at 4 C if not reading immediately; read
   within the window specified for the chemistry.

A generic template program is given in Appendix B; the assay-specific anneal
temperature and cycle number come from SOP-L701.

### Droplet Reading

1. Place the amplified, sealed plate in the QX200 Droplet Reader plate holder
   with the retaining clamp.
2. In QuantaSoft, set up the plate layout: sample names, assay/target names,
   fluorophores (FAM, HEX/VIC), experiment type (e.g., absolute
   quantification), and supermix/chemistry.
3. Start the run. The autosampler aspirates droplets well by well and the
   detector reads two channels per droplet.
4. Do not open the reader or disturb the plate while running.

### QuantaSoft Orientation (Reading the Output)

This is orientation only; thresholding decisions and full analysis are covered
in SOP-L702.

- **1-D plot:** fluorescence amplitude vs. droplet (event) number for one
  channel. Positive droplets sit above the threshold line; negatives below.
- **2-D plot:** channel 1 (FAM) vs. channel 2 (HEX/VIC) amplitude. In a duplex
  assay, droplets fall into four clusters: double-negative, FAM-only,
  HEX-only, and double-positive [@biorad_appsguide2018].
- **Thresholding:** the boundary between positive and negative clusters.
  Review it for every well; adjust manually in QuantaSoft Analysis Pro where
  the automatic call is poor.
- **Well merging:** replicate wells of the same sample/target may be merged to
  increase the effective partition count before concentration is calculated.
- **Concentration:** QuantaSoft reports copies per microliter from the Poisson
  fit. Export as described in SOP-L702, Section 6.1.

### Shutdown

1. Close the experiment and export/back up data (SOP-L702).
2. Remove and discard the plate and used cartridges/gaskets (Section 8).
3. Check and, if needed, empty the reader waste bottle.
4. Power down per the manual; leave the system in the state your lab specifies
   for the reader oil lines.

### Maintenance and Care

- **Each session:** check oil levels and the waste bottle; inspect for leaks.
- **Routine:** keep the reader's fluidics maintained per the manual; do not let
  oil bottles run dry mid-run.
- **Do not:** force cartridges or gaskets, reuse single-use consumables, mix
  oil chemistries, or use non-pierceable seals.
- **Records:** log each run (date, operator, assay, plate, instrument notes)
  and any maintenance or service in the instrument logbook.

### Troubleshooting

| Symptom                          | Likely cause                                  | Action                                                        |
|:---------------------------------|:----------------------------------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------------|
| Low accepted-droplet count       | Sheared droplets; pipetting too fast; bubbles | Pipette droplets slowly at an angle; avoid air; re-generate   |
| Few or no droplets generated     | Wrong/insufficient oil; cartridge/gasket seated poorly | Use matched oil; reseat cartridge and gasket           |
| "Rain" (droplets between clusters)| Suboptimal anneal temperature; degraded sample | Optimize anneal (SOP-L701); check DNA quality (SOP-L700)     |
| Reader error / clog              | Low oil; debris; fluidics issue               | Check oil and waste; run reader maintenance; see manual       |
| High NTC positives               | Contamination                                 | Rerun with fresh reagents; review setup (SOP-L702, Section 6.2)|


## Quality Control and Acceptance Criteria

- Each well should yield at least 10,000 accepted droplets (target ~12,000 to
  20,000); wells below 10,000 are excluded in analysis (SOP-L702).
- Run the controls defined in SOP-L702 (NTC, extraction blank, positive
  control) on every plate.
- Confirm uniform plate sealing and correct plate orientation before reading.
- Log instrument run metadata to support digital-PCR reporting standards
  [@dmiqe2020].


## Waste Disposal

- Used DG8 cartridges, gaskets, plates, foil, and tips: dispose as standard
  laboratory plastic/biohazard waste per the lab's waste plan.
- Generation and reader oil and oily waste: collect and dispose per the SDS and
  the lab's chemical-waste procedures; do not pour oil down the drain.
- Reagent containers: rinse and dispose per local guidance.

## Training Record

Before operating the QX200 system independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP and review the current Bio-Rad QX200 manual
   [@biorad_qx200_2024] and Applications Guide [@biorad_appsguide2018].
2. Read [SOP-L701 Primer Design](SOP-L701-ddpcr-nitrogen-cycle-primers.qmd) and
   [SOP-L702 Applications Guide](SOP-L702-ddpcr-applications-guide.qmd) for
   context on what they are running and why.
3. Observe a full run (generation, sealing, cycling, reading) performed by
   trained personnel.
4. Complete at least one full run under supervision, including QuantaSoft plate
   setup and export.
5. Be signed off by the PI or lab manager.

| Trainee | Date observed | Date supervised run | Signed off by | Date |
|:--------|:--------------|:--------------------|:--------------|:-----|
|         |               |                     |               |      |


## Appendix A: Pre-Run Checklist {.appendix}

- [ ] Validated reaction mix and plate plan ready (SOP-L701)
- [ ] Instruments powered on; QuantaSoft connected
- [ ] Generation oil matches supermix chemistry; sufficient volume
- [ ] Reader oil level adequate; waste bottle emptied
- [ ] DG8 cartridges, gaskets, plate, and pierceable foil on hand
- [ ] Controls included on the plate (NTC, extraction blank, positive control)
- [ ] PX1 sealer at correct temperature/time
- [ ] Thermal cycler ramp rate set to ~2 C/s
- [ ] Run logged in the instrument logbook


## Appendix B: Generic Thermal Cycling Template {.appendix}

Anneal/extension temperature and cycle number are assay-specific and come from
SOP-L701. The structure below is a starting template for probe-based ddPCR;
confirm against the supermix insert and current manual [@biorad_qx200_2024].

| Step                | Temperature | Time    | Cycles | Ramp     |
|:--------------------|:------------|:--------|:-------|:---------|
| Enzyme activation   | 95 C        | 10 min  | 1      | ~2 C/s   |
| Denaturation        | 94 C        | 30 s    | 39--40 | ~2 C/s   |
| Anneal/extension    | (assay)     | 1 min   | 39--40 | ~2 C/s   |
| Enzyme deactivation | 98 C        | 10 min  | 1      | ~2 C/s   |
| Hold                | 4 C         | hold    | 1      | ~2 C/s   |

::: {.callout-note}
EvaGreen chemistry uses a different supermix, oil, and cycling profile than
probe chemistry. If the lab runs EvaGreen assays, add a separate template here
once the standard profile is fixed in SOP-L701.
:::
